question: Do rounds 002-005's findings transfer from TopoShape to a real document?

environment.configuration: BUILD_GUI=OFF, BUILD_PART=ON, default parameters, no user preferences
environment.level: App::Document with Part::Box, Part::Cut, Part::Fillet and a real recompute()

measurements.name: PropertyLinkSub reference across a parameter change
measurements.result: resolved to the correct physical face (centre_x=30)
measurements.why_not_exercised: shadow_entries=1 but the mapped name was EMPTY, so the reference resolved through stable indexing, not the element map

measurements.name: Part::Fillet stays on the same physical corner
negative control: can the comparison distinguish two corners
which document features carry an element map

headline.finding: In this configuration no document-level Part feature carried an element map, so the identity layer measured across rounds 002-005 reached no consumer.
headline.source_confirmed_mechanism: Part::Box::execute assigns a raw TopoDS_Shape (this->Shape.setValue(ResultShape, false)); Part::Cut::execute does use makeElementShape, but booleans propagate maps from their inputs, so an unmapped input yields an unmapped result.
headline.consumer_side: PropertyLinkSub stored an empty mapped name and fell back to a raw index. Part::Fillet stores FilletElement { int edgeid; } - a raw index by design, with no name and no shadow.

what_still_worked: Both consumers survived the change and the save/reload anyway, because Part::Box's face and edge numbering is stable under a length change. The everyday path held - by stable indexing, not by the element map.
scope_limits: BUILD_GUI=OFF with default parameters and no user preferences. A GUI build with default preferences was not tested.
Part workbench only, with a chain starting from primitives. Sketcher and PartDesign are not built, and a chain starting from a Sketch was not tested - that is the obvious next question.
One change type (a length increase) on one shape family.
measurement_error_found_and_corrected: M2 first reported the fillet moving to a different corner. It had not: a fillet's cylindrical face centre sits inside its corner by a radius-dependent offset, and the expectation compared the face centre against the corner coordinates. The third such error in seven rounds.
